name: support
description: Long support/research conversation: facts given early, long pasted documents with buried details, drafting work, then recall probes.

turns.prompt: I'm the new support engineer for Halyard, our managed message-queue service. I'll give you context over several messages; keep it in mind for the whole conversation. First: the production cluster is hx-prod-amber and staging is hx-stg-cobalt. Broker ports: clients connect on 9092, the admin API is on 9644 and metrics on 9645. Acknowledge with a two-line summary.

Our biggest customer right now is Northwind Freight: account ACC-77341, Enterprise tier with a 99.95% SLA. Their contact is Hannah Okafor (platform lead). They have a custom retention of 240 hours; our default is 72 hours. Acknowledge briefly.

Last Tuesday's incident is INC-20931: a config push restarted consumer coordinators and caused a rebalance storm; delivery was delayed up to 26 minutes, no data loss. On-call this week is Priya Raman, and the escalation manager is Tomasz Wielki. Acknowledge briefly.
Explain in about 200 words how consumer-group rebalancing works and why a 'rebalance storm' happens.

Here are the 4.2.0 release notes. Summarise the five changes most relevant to Northwind.

{{truth.releaseNotes}}
Draft a short internal note for #halyard-ops about INC-20931: what happened, customer impact, follow-ups.

This is the broker override file for eu-west-1. Anything risky in here for a cluster that serves Northwind? Be concise.

{{truth.euWestConfig}}
What is a sensible max.poll.interval.ms for consumers that do slow database writes per batch? Give your reasoning in under 150 words.

Hannah just sent this. Summarise her asks as a numbered list.

{{truth.emailThread}}
Draft a reply to Hannah that answers her first three asks and confirms the call she asked for.

Here is our rolling-restart runbook. Turn it into a checklist of at most eight lines for tonight's maintenance on staging.

{{truth.runbook}}
Write the exact halyardctl command sequence to take broker 3 on staging out of service and bring it back, following the runbook.

Here is a lag export from the incident window. Which partition had the highest consumer lag, how high, and at what time?

{{truth.metricsCsv}}
Explain at-least-once versus exactly-once delivery in Halyard terms, in about 150 words.
Northwind's load test will run at 3x their normal peak. Using the numbers from Hannah's email, what message rate should we plan quotas for? Show the math in two lines.
Write a customer-facing FAQ entry: 'Why did my consumers stall during INC-20931?' Keep it under 120 words.
List five metrics we should alert on for Northwind's topics, each with a threshold.
Summarise everything we've covered so far in eight bullets.
What is Northwind Freight's account id and tier? Do not open files or run shell commands for this; memory tools are fine if you have them. Answer in one line.
What retention does Northwind have, and what is our default? Do not open files or run shell commands for this; memory tools are fine if you have them. Answer in one line.
What is the incident id of last Tuesday's incident? Do not open files or run shell commands for this; memory tools are fine if you have them. Answer in one line.
Which ports do the admin API and metrics use? Do not open files or run shell commands for this; memory tools are fine if you have them. Answer in one line.
In the eu-west-1 override file I pasted, what was replica.lag.max.ms set to? Do not open files or run shell commands for this; memory tools are fine if you have them. Answer in one line.
According to the 4.2.0 release notes, what is the new default for max.inflight.requests? Do not open files or run shell commands for this; memory tools are fine if you have them. Answer in one line.

When exactly did Hannah ask for the call? Do not open files or run shell commands for this; memory tools are fine if you have them. Answer in one line.
Who is on call this week and who is the escalation manager? Do not open files or run shell commands for this; memory tools are fine if you have them. Answer in one line.
